page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highcpu-64 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the c4d server family. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs based on the x86_64 CPU architecture, paired with 120.0 GB of system memory. This configuration yields a memory-to-core ratio of 1.88 GB per vCPU, prioritizing raw processing capacity over memory density.

This instance does not include integrated local storage or bundled GPU accelerators, meaning all storage requirements must be met via external network-attached block storage. Additionally, it does not provide complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent, non-shared compute resources for workloads requiring sustained processing power.

From a workload perspective, the high vCPU count and low memory-to-core ratio make this instance suitable for compute-intensive tasks such as batch processing, high-performance web serving, and distributed compute workloads that do not require massive memory footprints or local disk storage.
